KEY MESSAGE 1...A strong cold front will cross the region late 
this afternoon and this evening with severe weather possible.

Low pressure passing north of northern New England will drag a 
cold front through the region late this afternoon and evening. 
Clouds over the area are lifting and dissipating somewhat this 
afternoon, and it will warm up with highs in the upper 70s to 
low 80s. With clouds breaking up and sunshine developing, gusty 
southwest winds are ushering a more humid airmass into the area 
with surface dew points in the mid and upper 60s.

While instability values will be relatively low, generally 
SBCAPE values and MLCAPE values around 500 J/kg, but 06-km Bulk 
Shear will be upwards of 55-60 kt. SPC has the region in a 
Slight Risk (level 2 out of 5) for severe weather this afternoon
and evening, with part of the region now under a Severe
Thunderstorm Watch and the rest of the area likely to be added
to an additional watch later on. Timing looks to be around 4pm 
to 6pm for the southern Poconos, far northwest New Jersey, and 
the Lehigh Valley, 6pm to 8pm along the I-95 corridor, and from 
7pm to 9 pm over Delmarva and southern New Jersey. After sunset,
with loss of diurnal heating, the risk for severe weather will 
start to diminish.

A tight pressure gradient then develops over the area tonight
through Saturday as broad high pressure centered over the
Southern Plains begins to build east. Gusty north to northwest
winds will develop tonight and will continue through Saturday,
with winds ranging from 15 to 25 mph with 30 to 40 mph gusts. 
Much cooler on Saturday with highs in the 50s and surface dew 
points falling towards the 30s. Some showers may linger tonight
into Saturday morning especially across southern NJ and Delmarva
as the front slows for a time, but they should clear out finally
later in the day if not before.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Frost and freeze conditions are expected for 
Saturday night into Sunday morning with another round of frost 
possible for Sunday night into Monday morning.

The coldest airmass of the season thus far will usher into the 
region this weekend. With high pressure settling in from the north, 
skies will become clear by Saturday evening. While it will be a bit 
breezy early in the night, the pressure gradient is expected to 
lessen overnight, especially for locales north and west of I-95. In 
these areas, anticipate a period of good radiational cooling 
conditions where low temperatures are expected to fall into the 
upper 20s to low 30s. For this reason, have issued a Freeze Watch 
for potions of eastern PA and northern NJ for Saturday night. 
Further south and east, it appears that winds will remain elevated 
enough to preclude frost formation where temperatures will be in the 
mid to upper 30s. At this time, no frost/freeze headlines are 
expected along the I-95 corridor and points south and east. 

High temperatures on Sunday will then only be in the 50s for the 
entire region despite mostly sunny skies. Temperatures will then 
begin to slowly moderate Sunday night into early next week. Another 
round of frost/freeze conditions will be possible for Sunday night 
into Monday morning, mainly confined to the Lehigh Valley, Poconos 
and northern New Jersey. Lows are expected to be several degrees 
warmer than Saturday night mainly in the mid to upper 30s, so this 
would favor frost over freeze where the growing season remains 
active. Too early to determine any headlines at this time, but will 
be considered in future updates.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Uncertainty persists regarding a nor'easter 
developing off the coast of the southern Mid-Atlantic that may cause 
unsettled conditions and hazardous marine impacts early next week.

The base of a deep trough axis will pass through the region later 
Saturday. As it does so, the trough axis will then cutoff into an 
upper level low which will meander over the southern Mid-Atlantic 
coast into early next week. At the same time, strong and expansive 
high pressure will be building over the Ohio Valley. While 
confidence is increasing regarding a nor'easter developing off the 
North Carolina coast later this weekend, it must be said there 
remains a vast amount of uncertainty with regards to potential 
impacts to our region into next week. 

Considerable differences amongst global/ensemble guidance exists 
with regards to just how close/long this system will get/last in our 
region. Some guidance keeps the system suppressed further south due 
to the strong high to the north, which will then minimize potential 
impacts to our area. However, if the system is further north (and 
this has been the trend over the past 24 hours), then more in the 
way of impacts and unsettled weather may occur. At the very least, 
it is expected that gusty northeast breezes will occur for the 
majority of the week with the highest gusts located near coastal
